name: Linear regression and product moment correlation

questions.q: What does the Product Moment Correlation Coefficient measure?
a: The strength and direction of linear association between two variables
The rate of change of y with respect to x
The slope of the regression line
The goodness of fit of a quadratic curve

questions.q: What is the range of possible values for the Product Moment Correlation Coefficient r?
If the value of r is exactly -1, what does this indicate about the bivariate data points?
In the linear regression equation y = a + bx, what does the parameter b represent?
a: The gradient of the regression line

questions.q: How is the gradient b of the regression line y on x calculated using summary statistics Sxx and Sxy?
Through which notable point does every least squares regression line y = a + bx always pass?
a: The maximum x and maximum y

questions.q: Given that Sxx = 100, Syy = 144, and Sxy = 120, calculate the Product Moment Correlation Coefficient r.
What is meant by the term interpolation when using a regression line?
a: Predicting a value outside the range of the given data set
Estimating a value of y for a given x that is well above maximum data
Estimating a value of y for an x value that lies within the range of observed data

questions.q: Why is extrapolation using a regression line generally considered unreliable?
a: The linear relationship may not hold outside the range of observed data
It changes the value of Sxy
It violates the definition of PMCC

questions.q: If r = 0.85, what percentage of the variation in y can be explained by the linear relationship with x?

a: r changes sign if scaling factor is negative

Which of the following scatter diagrams would produce a PMCC close to zero?
a: Points forming a steep upward straight line
Points forming a downward straight line
Points forming a tight exponential curve
Points scattered randomly with no discernible pattern

questions.q: What is a residual in regression analysis?
a: The difference between the observed value of y and the predicted value from the regression line
The sum of all x values divided by n
The slope of the regression line

questions.q: If Sxx = 80, Syy = 45, and Sxy = -50, what can be deduced about the relationship between x and y?
a: x and y are positively correlated
x and y are negatively correlated
x and y are perfectly uncorrelated

questions.q: In least squares regression, what quantity is minimized to find the best-fit line?
a: The product of Sxx and Syy

a: Both variables must follow a bivariate normal distribution
The data must be time-series data
The variance of x must equal variance of y
The sample size must be exactly 30

questions.q: Given Sxy = 240, Sxx = 300, Syy = 200, calculate the gradient b of the regression line of y on x.
What does a negative value of the regression coefficient b signify?
a: As x increases, y tends to increase
As x increases, y tends to decrease

questions.q: If r = 0.9, what is the coefficient of determination, and what does it represent?
a: 0.81, meaning 81 percent of the variance in y is explained by x

questions.q: When should you use the regression line of x on y rather than y on x?
a: When x is independent and y is dependent
When estimating x for a given value of y

Outliers can severely distort the value of r

What is the primary limitation of the Product Moment Correlation Coefficient?
a: It cannot be calculated for samples greater than 100

It requires both variables to have a mean of zero
It is only valid for discrete probability distributions
